objectives.statement: Represent fractions, including fractions equal to or greater than 1, on area models and a number line, naming the whole each fraction refers to.
Add and subtract fractions with like denominators, and with related denominators (e.g. halves, quarters, eighths), by using equivalent fractions.
Compare and order fractions using benchmarks (0, 1/2, 1), common denominators and the number line, and justify each comparison.

content.body: Synthetic sharing demonstration. A fraction measures equal parts of one fixed whole. Repartitioning changes the names of the parts without changing the amount. Compare two thirds and three quarters only when the wholes have the same size.

accessibility.textAlternative: Synthetic sharing demonstration. A fraction measures equal parts of one fixed whole. Repartitioning changes the names of the parts without changing the amount. Compare two thirds and three quarters only when the wholes have the same size. A bar split into 3 equal parts with 2 shaded: 2/3. Split a whole into equal parts. 2/3 is the same amount as 4/6, 8/12. Multiply the count of parts and the count of equal pieces by the same factor.

content.body: A denominator names the unit being counted. Use equal-sized pieces before combining or comparing their counts. The size of the whole stays fixed.

accessibility.textAlternative: A denominator names the unit being counted. Use equal-sized pieces before combining or comparing their counts. The size of the whole stays fixed. Compare 2/3 and 3/4. Step 1: Use twelfths for both quantities. 2/3 = 8/12, 3/4 = 9/12 Step 2: With the same unit, compare the counts. 8/12 < 9/12 Add one half and one quarter. Step 1: Rename one half as two quarters. 1/2 = 2/4 Step 2: Count quarters, keeping the size of the pieces. 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4

content.body: Synthetic seed-bank task. A group has three quarters of a kilogram of seed and packs one third of a kilogram for a new garden.

prompts.prompt: Explain how a common unit lets you subtract these quantities, and why the remainder must be smaller than three quarters.
